subject: Social Habits
title: Working together
objectives: Children will work with a friend or a small group on a simple task.
content: Building together, carrying together, and group games.
teachingActivities: Choose tasks that need two or more children; give each child a clear part; praise the team ("We did it"); keep groups small; step back as children cooperate; rotate partners.
learnerActivities: Work with a friend on a simple task and say "we did it".
assessment: Observe whether each child works with a friend on a simple task and joins a group game.
expectedOutcomes: Works with a friend on a simple task.

lessons.title: Building together
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will build something together with a friend.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can try new things and calm big feelings.
lessons.starter: Show a pile of blocks and say "One child can build a little. Two children can build a lot."
teacherActivities: Show how two children pass blocks to build a wall.
Pair children and give them blocks.
learnerActivities: Child says a word or points.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how two children pass blocks to build a wall. Children: Children watch.
Step 2. Teacher: Pair children and give them blocks. Children: Child builds with a friend.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "What are you building?" Children: Child says a word or points.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "We built it together." Children: Children repeat the sentence.

practical.title: Build a wall
practical.safety: Use large light blocks only and keep towers low. Seat children safely and supervise closely.

differentiation.extension: Ask the pair to name what they built.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Look at the building and say "Well done, team."
lessons.homeConnection: Build with blocks together at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "build something together with a friend" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Together, together, we can do it together.

lessons.title: Carrying together
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will carry a light object together.
successCriteria: Carries a light object with a friend
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can try new things and calm big feelings.
lessons.starter: Show a light box and say "It is too big for one. Two children can carry it."
teacherActivities: Show how two children hold opposite sides.
Pair children and let them carry the box.
learnerActivities: Child carries the box with a friend.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how two children hold opposite sides. Children: Children watch.
Step 2. Teacher: Pair children and let them carry the box. Children: Child carries the box with a friend.
Step 3. Teacher: Walk slowly across the room. Children: Children walk together.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "We carried it together." Children: Children repeat the sentence.

practical.title: Carry the box
steps: Hold the box with a friend.
practical.safety: Use a very light box and keep the route clear. Supervise every pair and never carry anything heavy.

differentiation.support: Carry the box together with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the pair to carry the box around a cone.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Was it too big for one?

lessons.conclusion: Put the box away and say "Team."
lessons.homeConnection: Carry light things together at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "carry a light object together" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Group games
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will join a group game and cooperate.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can try new things and calm big feelings.
lessons.starter: Hold the cloth and say "Hold on tight. Everyone together."
teacherActivities: Show how to hold the cloth edge and lift together.
Lift and lower the cloth with a song.
Roll a ball on the cloth.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to hold the cloth edge and lift together. Children: Children hold the cloth.
Step 2. Teacher: Lift and lower the cloth with a song. Children: Children lift together.
Step 3. Teacher: Roll a ball on the cloth. Children: Children watch and shake gently.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "We played together." Children: Children cheer.

practical.title: Cloth game
practical.safety: Use a soft light cloth and a very soft ball. Keep the group small and away from furniture.

differentiation.support: Hold the cloth beside the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to lead the lifting count.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Fold the cloth and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Play a simple group game with the family.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "join a group game and cooperate" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Team project
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will complete a small project together.
successCriteria: Works with others to finish a project
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can try new things and calm big feelings.
lessons.starter: Show a large sheet of paper and say "Today we make one big picture together."
teacherActivities: Put the paper on the floor and show each child a space.
Let children add colour or collage materials.
Hang the picture and say "We made it together."
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Put the paper on the floor and show each child a space. Children: Children choose a space.
Step 2. Teacher: Let children add colour or collage materials. Children: Child adds to the picture.
Step 3. Teacher: Talk about the picture. Children: Child says what they added.
Step 4. Teacher: Hang the picture and say "We made it together." Children: Children cheer.

practical.title: Team picture
practical.safety: Use non-toxic washable materials and supervise closely. Keep small items out of mouths.

differentiation.support: Add your part beside the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say what their part is.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.homeConnection: Make a picture together as a family.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "complete a small project together" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 3 teamwork check
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child works with others.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can try new things and calm big feelings.
lessons.starter: Sing the teamwork song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: build, carry and cloth.
At each station watch how children cooperate.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: build, carry and cloth. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station watch how children cooperate. Children: Child works with a friend.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Teamwork stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station closely and keep floors clear. Use light objects only.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one station.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to include a quiet friend.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: builds with a friend; carries with a friend; joins a group game; says we did it.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 3
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep doing things together at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child works with others" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
